claim: Sergeant Jacob Zorn applied a "wristlock" maneuver to Shela Linton.
evidence: Sergeant Jacob Zorn used a “ ‘pain compliance tech - nique’ ” called a rear wristlock on Shela Linton, a nonviolent protestor who was peacefully demonstrating at a sit-in in the Vermont capitol.
excerpt: Sergeant Jacob Zorn used a “ ‘pain compliance tech - nique’ ” called a rear wristlock on Shela Linton, a nonviolent protestor who was peacefully demonstrating at a sit-in in the Vermont capitol. 135 F. 4th 19, 24–25 CA2 (2025). The Second Circuit held that Zorn was not entitled to qualified immunity on Linton’s Fourth Amendment excessive force claim, at least at the summary judgment stage, because prior Circuit precedent had clearly established that using a rear wristlock against a nonviolent protestor would violate the protestor’s constitutional rights.
